target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures focus on the company's global pay equity achievements and analysis processes. The 2023 disclosure (mu_2023_1_D074) highlights achieving global pay equity for underrepresented employees in bonuses and stock rewards in 2023 (with base pay increases suspended) and notes a 2024 analysis. The 2024 disclosure (mu_2024_1_D083) confirms achieving global pay equity for all underrepresented employees in 2024 across base pay and stock rewards. While the specific components of equity achievement changed (from bonuses/stock to base/stock), the underlying topic of global pay equity performance and analysis remains consistent.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD invests in competitive salaries, incentives, and benefits to attract and retain talent, regularly reviewing compensation practices and benchmarking pay ranges against market data to ensure equitable pay based on role, experience, skills, and performance.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies emphasize regular reviews of compensation to ensure equity, though AMD explicitly mentions benchmarking against market data while MU reports a specific achievement of global pay equity for underrepresented employees. AMD states it 'regularly review[s] our compensation practices... ensuring equitable pay' and 'benchmark set pay ranges based on relevant market data', whereas MU highlights that it 'achieved global pay equity for all underrepresented employees in compensation' through regular reviews of base pay and stock awards.

sentences.text: We have a regular review of pay globally, including base pay and stock awards, to drive compensation equitably.
In 2024, we achieved global pay equity for all underrepresented employees in compensation across base pay and stock rewards.
We regularly review our compensation practices, considering factors relevant to ensuring equitable pay such as an employee's role, experience, skills, and performance.
We also benchmark set pay ranges based on relevant market data and our overall workforce.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company's global voluntary attrition rate was approximately 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), both below the technology industry benchmark from AON's 2024 study.
comparisons.comparison: While both companies focus on human capital metrics to assess employee experience, MU focuses on proactive pay equity and benefits inclusivity, whereas AVGO focuses on voluntary attrition rates as a primary measure of engagement and retention. MU reports on achieving pay equity and assessing benefits for inclusion, while AVGO reports specific attrition percentages (2.9% and 6.2%) benchmarked against industry standards to measure engagement.

sentences.text: We have a regular review of pay globally, including base pay and stock awards, to drive compensation equitably.
We plan to also continually assess our global leave, medical, and financial benefits to ensure market competitiveness and opportunities to create greater inclusion.
We measure our employees' engagement by our voluntary attrition rate and employee feedback.

Our global voluntary attrition rates in fiscal year 2024 were approximately 2.9% (excluding employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger) and approximately 6.2% (including employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger), which are both below the technology industry benchmark (AON, 2024 Salary Increase and Turnover Study - Second Edition, September 2024).

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel has maintained global gender pay equity and US race/ethnicity pay equity since 2019 by closing pay gaps after accounting for legitimate business factors, and publicly releases EEO-1 survey pay data for transparency.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific achievements in global pay equity, but INTC maintains a longer-standing record covering gender (globally) and race/ethnicity (in the US) since 2019, while MU reports achieving pay equity for 'underrepresented employees' in 2024. INTC explicitly details closing gaps after accounting for business factors like tenure and location, and mentions public transparency via EEO-1 data, whereas MU focuses on the outcome of equity in base pay and stock rewards without detailing the statistical methodology or transparency reporting.

sentences.text: In 2024, we achieved global pay equity for all underrepresented employees in compensation across base pay and stock rewards.
We have a regular review of pay globally, including base pay and stock awards, to drive compensation equitably.
Since 2019, we have achieved gender pay equity globally and we continue to maintain race/ethnicity pay equity in the US.

We achieve pay equity by closing the gap in average pay between employees of different genders or race/ethnicity in the same or similar roles after accounting for legitimate business factors that can explain differences, such as location, time at grade level, and tenure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Initiatives
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA is committed to creating an inclusive culture and building a diverse talent pipeline, particularly for women and underrepresented minorities in technology. To achieve this, the company partners with diverse institutions, embeds recruiting teams, supports women's leadership development, provides executive sponsors, trains managers on diversity, and tracks metrics on retention, pay, and engagement.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies link equity efforts to diversity and inclusion strategies for underrepresented groups. NVDA tracks 'equity and parity in retention, promotions, pay' as part of its broader DEI strategy to build diverse pipelines, while MU reports achieving 'global pay equity for all underrepresented employees' as a specific outcome of its regular pay reviews. NVDA's approach is broader, encompassing recruitment and retention metrics alongside pay, whereas MU's disclosure is centered on the compensation adjustment outcome itself.

sentences.text: In 2024, we achieved global pay equity for all underrepresented employees in compensation across base pay and stock rewards.
• Track equity and parity in retention, promotions, pay, and employee engagement scores; and

When recruiting for new talent or developing our current employees, we strive to build a diverse talent pipeline that includes those underrepresented in the technology field, including women, Black/African American, and Hispanic/Latino candidates.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualmond provides robust compensation and benefits including salaries, bonuses, stock awards, retirement plans, healthcare, paid time off, family leave, and on-site services, tailored by country/region.

QCOM's disclosure is descriptive of the 'robust' program offerings, while MU's is declarative of a diversity metric success.

We provide robust compensation and benefits programs to help meet the needs of our employees.

In addition to salaries, these programs may include (depending on country/region) annual bonuses, stock awards, an employee stock purchase plan, retirement and savings plans, healthcare and insurance benefits, health savings and flexible spending accounts, paid time off, family leave, family care resources, flexible work schedules, adoption and surrogacy assistance, employee assistance programs, tuition assistance, and on-site services such as health and fitness centers, among others.
